text.p: The Netherlands' Philips Electronics NV rose Wednesday above a 12-month high to highlight trade in American depositary receipts (ADRs).
Philips was up 4-3/4 from its Tuesday close, itself a 12-month high, to 70-7/8. Volume was moderate and the company's ADRs were among percentage gain leaders on the New York Stock Exchange.

The increase followed Tuesday's announcement that Philips and the United States' Lucent Technologies Inc were combining their consumer telephone and related businesses in a joint venture with annual sales of about $2.5 billion. Lucent was up 1/8 to 70.

British Sky Broadcasting Group Plc was off 3-3/4 to 52-3/8 after the Financial Times newspaper reported the company could be shut out of bidding for new digital television licenses. British Sky was among percentage loss leaders on the New York Stock Exchange.
Swedish telephone equipment company Telefon AB L.M. Ericsson eased 3/16 to 38-1/4. The company's ADRs were among the most active on New York exchanges.

Among Latin American ADRs, Brazilian telephone company Telebras SA was up one to 144-1/8. Morgan Stanley said Wednesday it kept its strong buy rating on the ADRs and set a new 12-month price target of $180 an ADR.
The lower house of Brazil's Congress is scheduled to vote Wednesday on a bill regulating Brazil's telecom sector and outlining the privatization of the state-run Telebras system.
Decliners led advancers 217 to 154 among 814 ADRs. The ADR group was off 0.08 percent in mid-morning and volume was 17.3 million shares.
